name: Briar Henry
home: the blocks north of the port
life: “I still remember building a tiny table from leftover porch boards.” People around the market by Market Flats know Briar by a small Thursday habit. Briar often waits until the delivery baskets are stacked before going in.
voice: I was coming to fix the porch rail and ended up assembling a folding lunch table for three.
appearance: Briar is easy to recognize by brown hair pinned away from the temples and a broad nose and a deep dimple on one cheek. Usually dressed in a plum-colored cardigan with a pair of reading glasses in a cloth sleeve, Briar holds eye contact until the other person has finished when listening.
personality: Briar takes a rejection personally for a day and analytically on the second morning. Briar can be generous with a rival once the first night's sleep has intervened.
agenda: To leave a table that seats three.
family: Ada Firth is Briar’s older relative by marriage. Briar calls back when there is finally a little privacy. Ada leaves the first voice message. In their family a missed ring can mean a bus, a customer, a sleeping child or a bad hour. Neither treats it as an answer in itself. Asked about *A tide at noon*, Ada says, “I found the old finish flag under the new tide.”
connections: Mateo Adair. A folding table and a walk to the corner both make the extra half hour count.
